newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA DELAYS RULING ON SLAVYANI BANK INSOLVENCY.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA DELAYS RULING ON SLAVYANI BANK INSOLVENCY.

text.p: The Sofia City Court postponed ruling on an insolvency case against private Slavyani bank by three weeks due to delayed preparation of experts' statement on its financial state, a bank official said on Tuesday.
"The court postponed ruling on the case for June 3 because the financial experts it has appointed failed to submit their report in due time," the official, who declined to be named told Reuters.

The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) put Slavyani bank in receivership on September 23 due to a danger of insolvency, citing a capital-to-risk assets ratio of minus 38.67 percent and oustanding payments of 223 million levs.
The BNB decided to seek the bank's insolvency on October 30.

So far Bulgarian courts have declared bankrupt four banks out of a total of 17 private and state owned institutions or a third of the country's banks, whose insolvency has been sought by the BNB in several waves since May 1996.
These were the private Crystalbank, the Private Agricultural and Investment Bank, private Trade and Savings Bank and the state-owned Mineralbank.
Of the 17 banks only private Mollov bank, now named Eurobank avoided bankruptcy after Slovak investment fund Istrocapital invested $6.25 million in it to acquire some 90 percent of its capital.

Under a funding agreement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) sealed in March Bulgaria is to amend its legislation to speed up bankruptcy procedures for banks whose insolvency has been ascertained by the BNB.

Under a new Banking Act draft, pending a government approval courts would be required to rule on bank bankruptcy cases not later than 30 days after the BNB files the suit and would not be able to appoint experts to prepare independent reports on the banks' financial state.
Delayed reports by court experts have been cited as the reason for postponement of ruling on most bank bankruptcy cases so far. -- Roumiana Tikholova, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88
